Summary view with SLOOS and Beige Book overlay:
- Policy stance: Cautiously hawkish. The FOMC held the funds rate at 4.25–4.50% and continued balance-sheet runoff, citing solid activity, low/stable unemployment, and still-elevated inflation alongside rising two‑sided risks.
- Beige Book (April 2025) signal: District contacts generally described overall activity as flat to modest, with mixed consumer spending (non-essentials softer), manufacturing little changed, and residential real estate constrained by affordability/inventory. Labor markets remained tight but showed further easing in hiring conditions and slower wage growth. Price increases were described as modest to moderate with some deceleration and less pricing power; input cost pressures eased. Credit conditions tightened further; CRE—especially office—remained weak. Outlooks were cautious with elevated uncertainty.
- SLOOS (April 2025) signal: Banks tightened standards and saw weaker loan demand across C&I/CRE; foreign/other banks tightened notably. Reasons included weaker outlook and lower risk tolerance.

Implications: Beige Book and SLOOS both point to tighter credit, soft CRE, easing wage/price pressures, and slower underlying momentum than suggested by “solid” headline activity. This leans against additional tightening and supports patience, nudging the overall read modestly dovish versus the statement alone.

Net assessment: Maintain a restrictive stance given still-elevated inflation, but Beige Book- and SLOOS‑indicated headwinds and cooling pressures shift the balance further toward neutral/slightly dovish.
